architectureCatalog.name: MVC
architectureCatalog.description: Model-View-Controller pattern separating internal representations of information from user interface.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Monolithic web applications, simple to medium complexity CRUD systems.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Views depend on Models; Controllers orchestrate Model and View interaction.

architectureCatalog.name: Repository + Service
architectureCatalog.description: Layered architecture separating data access logic (Repository) from business rules (Service) and transport (Controller/Handler).
architectureCatalog.useCase: Standard enterprise REST APIs and web services with moderate business logic.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Upper layers depend on lower layer interfaces; data access is decoupled from controllers.

architectureCatalog.name: Clean Architecture
architectureCatalog.description: Hexagonal / Onion inspired architecture putting Domain Entities and Use Cases at the core with dependency inversion.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Complex domain logic, long-lifecycle systems needing framework independence and testability.
architectureCatalog.projectStructure: Domain -> Use Cases -> Interface Adapters -> Frameworks & Drivers
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Source code dependencies point inwards only. Domain entities know nothing of external systems.

architectureCatalog.name: Modular Monolith
architectureCatalog.description: Single deployable unit structured strictly into bounded modules with clear public APIs and isolated schemas.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Scaling development across multiple teams while avoiding premature microservices complexity.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Modules only interact via public contracts/interfaces or asynchronous events.

deploymentCatalog.name: Docker
deploymentCatalog.description: Container platform providing lightweight virtualization to package applications and dependencies into standardized containers.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Local development, reproducible testing environments, and standard deployment artifacts.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Code -> Build Image -> Tag -> Push to Registry -> Run Container

deploymentCatalog.name: Docker Compose
deploymentCatalog.description: Multi-container orchestration tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications via YAML specification.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Small to medium self-hosted deployments, staging environments, developer local setups.
disadvantages: Limited automated scaling and zero-downtime rolling updates compared to K8s

deploymentCatalog.name: Windows Service
deploymentCatalog.description: Long-running executable applications that run in their own Windows session without requiring a logged-in user.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: On-premise enterprise Windows environments, legacy integration, local hardware daemon.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Publish binary -> Register Service (sc create / nssm) -> Start Service

deploymentCatalog.name: Linux Service (systemd)
deploymentCatalog.description: System and service manager for Linux operating systems providing process supervision and logging.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Bare-metal or VPS Linux deployments for compiled binaries (Go, Rust, .NET Core) or Node daemons.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Copy binary -> Write /etc/systemd/system/app.service -> systemctl daemon-reload -> systemctl enable --now app

levels.description: Most detailed diagnostic messages containing full payloads and step-by-step state.
Information useful during development and debugging sessions.
Normal operational events tracking general flow of application.
Unexpected events or degraded performance that did not stop execution.
Failures and exceptions that prevent standard operation of a specific request.
Severe failures requiring immediate system-wide attention or causing service outage.

authentication.name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
authentication.description: Stateless token authentication with signed claims, short expiration, and refresh token rotation.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Industry-standard authorization framework enabling third-party and federated login.

authentication.name: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
authentication.description: Identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 for single sign-on (SSO) and user identity verification.

authorization.name: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)
authorization.description: Permissions assigned to roles (Admin, Member, Viewer); users are assigned to roles.

authorization.name: Permission-Based (Fine-Grained)
authorization.description: Granular capability flags (e.g., project:create, user:delete) evaluated per request.

applicationSecurity.name: HTTPS Everywhere
applicationSecurity.description: Enforce TLS 1.3 encryption for all data in transit; redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

applicationSecurity.name: Password Hashing
applicationSecurity.description: Use modern adaptive hashing algorithms like Argon2id or Bcrypt with adequate work factors.

applicationSecurity.name: Input Validation & Sanitization
applicationSecurity.description: Strict schema validation (Zod, FluentValidation, Joi) on all client and API inputs.

applicationSecurity.name: CORS Policy
applicationSecurity.description: Explicit origin whitelisting; avoid wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with credentials.

applicationSecurity.name: Rate Limiting
applicationSecurity.description: Protect public endpoints and authentication routes against brute-force and DDoS.

applicationSecurity.name: SQL Injection Prevention
applicationSecurity.description: Always use parameterized queries or trusted ORMs; never concatenate raw SQL strings.

applicationSecurity.name: XSS & CSRF Protection
applicationSecurity.description: Content Security Policy (CSP), HttpOnly + SameSite cookies, and output encoding.

rules: Never commit secrets, passwords, or connection strings into git repositories.
Use environment variables or cloud secret managers (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault).
Rotate secrets and API keys periodically.
